[L3] Both sides answered the witnesses pressed against their links in their link rounds. [L4] The mechanism question -- whether the timing rows of Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 1:34-35 exclude Joseph as begetter -- is inference on both sides, each footed on the forms, so no link was refuted from the text and none was withdrawn.
RESULT: UNDERDETERMINED -- Both readings stand on exhibited layers of the same verses, so the text as argued here does not settle whether Joseph begat the child or the Holy Ghost's conception excluded a man.

CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 0 -- all six defender-listed premises are spared: every [DR3] entry exhibits [L1]+[L2] (and [L3]) footing and shows its chain, so none is CONCEDED and none UNEXHIBITED.

D1 vs C5 (Luke 3:23): UNDERDETERMINED -- the defender named and answered the pressed qualifier (enomizeto, answered by Acts 16:13) and the naming rows stand as text; the defender left Luke 2:44 and Acts 14:19 unnamed, but those usage-parallels interpret the qualifier, they do not state a denial of the naming, and the challenger's supposition reading meets the defender's wont-parallel as footed inference on both sides.
D2: STANDS -- the challenger never contradicted that the seed rows speak a flesh seed out of a father's body; the dispute over whether the line reaches Joseph is D6's load.
D3 vs C1/C2/C3 (Matthew 1:16-25; Luke 1:34): UNDERDETERMINED -- the defender named and answered Matthew 1:18, 1:25, Genesis 4:1 and 4:25 and Luke 1:34-35 in [CR2] and [CR3] LINK 3 and LINK 6; the timing rows and the non-narration reading each keep their footing.
D4 vs C3/C4 (Luke 1:35; John 1:13; Matthew 1:3-6): UNDERDETERMINED -- the defender named and answered the ek-of-the-mother rows (Matthew 1:3-6, inside active begetting verses) and John 1:13 in [CR3] LINKS 3-4; both ek readings stand as inference from exhibited forms.
D5 vs challenger LINK 6 (1 Chronicles 2:34-35): UNDERDETERMINED -- the defender named the row and answered that it names the begetter (Jarha) while reckoning to Sheshan's house; whether house-reckoning proves biology stays open.
D6 vs C7: UNDERDETERMINED -- every pressed witness (Matthew 1:18-25, Luke 1:34-35, Genesis 4:1/4:25, Jeremiah 22:30, Galatians 4:4, Romans 1:3) was named and answered in [CR3]; both conclusions are inference from footed rows, and Isaiah 28:10's chain scope bars demanding a single stating verse for either.
CITATION CHECK: the challenger's [DR1] quote of Judges 11:39 as "have not known man" is a citation error -- the wording is not found in Judges (the verse reads "she knew no man") -- and it is not [L1] footing for the vow parallel; the defender's [CR2] line "a just man does not put away the mother of his own child" attributed to Matthew 1:19 is the flagged wording-not-found case, but it was the defender quoting the challenger's own [L4] inference, not defender evidence. No unserved conclusion or sight labels were cited by either side.
OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS:
DEFENDER | CR2 | "My case does not narrate a mechanism either; the text names a father and requires a flesh seed."
CHALLENGER | DR2 | "I grant that the text never says in so many words that Luke 3:27's Salathiel is Matthew 1:12's."
DEFENDER CHAIN MARK: FOOTED -- every load-bearing link D1-D6 is footed on exhibited [L1] rows with [L2] forms in [CR3], the decisive load being D6's seed rows (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3) plus the five named registers.
CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK: FOOTED -- the challenger's alternative reading is carried by [L1]+[L2]+[L3] exhibits in [DR3], the decisive load being its Matthew 1:18/1:25 timing chain with the Genesis 4:1 idiom and the ek source rows of Matthew 1:3-6."}
